First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int \frac{1}{{k}^{2}+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{k}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{k})+C
$$

We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{6}{{z}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}z & =6\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{1}{{z}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}z \\  & =6\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{1}{{z}^{2}+{3}^{2}}\,\text{d}z \\  & =6\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{z}{3})]}_{a}^{0} \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡0-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{3})) \\  & =2\cdot (0-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{3})).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3}),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3})=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3})=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/a4961fa6f4f1aafeba2e8f77ed91e7d034fffd6aa249f13bb8357da11a7cea5e.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{6}{{z}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}z & =2\cdot (0-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{3})) \\  & =2\cdot (0-(-\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
